meal.title: Time Sharing Basics
meal.objective: Describe how multiple processes share a CPU over time

voice.script: What if your computer could multitask in a heartbeat? How does one CPU let many programs run seemingly at once? Time sharing means the operating system gives each process a tiny slice of CPU time, then moves to the next, repeating in a loop. The code below shows a list of process names and a loop that prints which one runs for each slice. When you run it, you’ll see the CPU jumping from Process A to Process B to Process C over and over. That rapid rotation is what lets many processes use the CPU quickly. Try changing the slice order or adding another process to see the effect.
